data.name: Bhari
data.gender_notes: Bhari is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhari is derived from the Sanskrit word bharati, which means ‘to carry’ or ‘to bear’. This name is often given to a girl who is expected to carry the weight of her responsibilities and family duties with strength and grace. The name Bhari carries the meaning “Strong, Powerful” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhari usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, powerful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner strength and resilience of a woman.
data.etymology: Bhari belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong, Powerful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhari total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

It is a reminder that even the heaviest of burdens can be borne with the strength of the human spirit and the support of a higher power. vedic_reference.note: Bhari is a name mentioned in various Vedic texts and is considered a divine name. It is also the name of Bhari Rishi, a sage mentioned in the Mahabharata.

historical_references.reference: Bhari was a name given to the goddess Durga during the Durga Puja festival in Bengal, India. The name signifies the goddess in her form as the mother who provides nourishment and protection.
historical_references.context: Durga Puja is a major festival in the Hindu calendar celebrated in the fall where the goddess Durga is worshipped and offerings are made to her in the form of clay idols. The festival is believed to mark the triumph of good over evil.

historical_references.reference: Bhari was also a name given to a legendary king of the Chalukya dynasty in the Deccan region of India. He is known for his valor and his conquest of the Western Gangas.
historical_references.context: The Chalukya Empire was a major power in the Deccan region of India during the medieval period. Bhari, as the king, contributed significantly to the expansion of the Chalukya Empire.
